Cassie: Opened a docs PR to standardize telemetry field names and add audit-export redaction examples: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/1301
Alex: 👍 are we renaming fields or just adding examples?
Cassie: Both. Examples will use "pseudonymous_id" and an explicit "tenant_id". Also adding pre-export redaction snippets showing HMAC hashing with a KMS-managed salt and an allowlist pattern for routing keys.
Jordan: Can you paste the short Go snippet so I can mirror it in the runtime hook?
Cassie: In the PR description I added this minimal example:
```
// redactEvent hashes tenant_id and strips free-text before export
func redactEvent(evt map[string]interface{}, salt string) map[string]interface{} {
  if v, ok := evt["tenant_id"].(string); ok {
    mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, []byte(salt))
    mac.Write([]byte(v))
    evt["tenant_id"] = fmt.Sprintf("hmac:%x", mac.Sum(nil))
  }
  delete(evt, "raw_prompt")
  delete(evt, "user_message")
  return evt
}
```
Maria: Small wording ask from Legal: avoid the acronym "PII" in public docs. Use "sensitive identifiers" and list examples.
Lee (Compliance): Agreed. Also call out that routing keys (region, shard) must not be redacted so metrics and routing remain intact. Show an allowlist in snippets and reference the central Audit Retention page rather than giving TTLs.
Cassie: Added an allowlist comment and a TypeScript minimal redact example that copies only allowed keys and scrubs email-like tokens. Left a TODO for a unit test in the PR.
Jordan: I opened a follow-up PR with a tiny unit test for the TS snippet and linked it back: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/1302
Alex: I'll run compile + lint on the Go snippet tomorrow AM. Keep imports minimal.
Cassie: Thanks. I'll re-run the snippet linter before merge and tag Compliance for final language sign-off.
Lee (Compliance): Please include a "Compliance sign-off required" checkbox in the PR template. Also ensure the snippet mentions KMS for salt lifecycle.
Cassie: Done in the PR body and template. Tagging reviewers @Lee (Compliance) and @Alex.
